content.title: ‘The Boys’ Cast Reacts To A-Train's Season 5 Premiere Death
content.text: Tomer Capone as Frenchie, Karen Fukuhara as Kimiko, Karl Urban as Billy Butcher, Erin Moriarty as Annie January/Starlight and Jack Quaid as Hughie Campbell.Jasper Savage/Prime VideoWarning: Spoilers ahead for season five, episode one of The Boys.The fifth and final season of The Boys has claimed its first major victim: A-Train.The Boys returned on Wednesday, picking up one year after the season four finale, in which Billy Butcher (Karl Urban) drove off with the supe-killing virus, Hughie Campbell (Jack Quaid), Mother’s Milk (Laz Alonso), Frenchie (Tomer Capone) and Kimiko (Karen Fukuhara) were captured by Vought, Annie January/Starlight (Erin Moriarty) fled and Homelander (Antony Starr) gained full control of the US government. In the season five premiere (“Fifteen Inches of Sheer Dynamite”), Homelander announces the execution of Hughie, MM and Frenchie, prompting Butcher to team up with Annie and Kimiko to rescue the guys from a Vought-run “Freedom Camp” before time runs out. To add more firepower to their rescue efforts, Annie reaches out to A-Train (Jessie T. Usher), but he turns her down, fearful for his life and that of his family members. His reluctance is understandable, considering that in season four, A-Train flipped sides to join The Boys and escaped before Homelander could confront him about his betrayal. “I remember having a conversation with Eric [Kripke] where I realized that A-Train was severing enough ties and backing himself into a tight enough corner that I did not see a way out for him,” Usher said while joined by showrunner Eric Kripke and Starr during a recent pre-premiere interview. Jessie T. Usher as A-Train on the season five premiere of "The Boys."Jasper Savage/Prime VideoA-Train is killed by Homelander in the final moment of the season five premiere. But before that, his redemption arc comes full circle when he arrives at the camp just in time to save Hughie from being on the receiving end of Homelander’s deadly laser eye-beams. “When you go back to the pilot, in the first five minutes, he murders Robin and sets the entire story in motion by ruining Hughie’s life,” Kripke said. “So to really bring things full circle and to show how far he’s come, we thought it was important for him to save Hughie's life.”In another nod to A-Train’s evolution, as the speedster runs from Homelander, he sees a woman in his path and moves out of the way to avoid killing her. In doing so, he becomes off-balance and crashes into the woods. Forbes‘The Boys’ Season 5 Premiere Recap: No One Is Safe In Homelander’s AmericaHomelander catches up to him and in the ensuing face-off, a now fearless A-Train laughs in his face, calling the egomaniac supe a loser who would be nothing without his powers. Reaching a breaking point, Homelander snaps A-Train’s neck and kills him. “The fact that he was able to admit a lot of things to himself and to Homelander in that final moment was just the most important and impactful decision that I think A-Train has ever made in this show,” Usher said. In many ways, it was fitting that Homelander was the character responsible for the tragedy. “I felt relieved and thankful that I was able to have Antony as a scene partner for that final moment because he’s been the monster that's been daunting A-Train from the very beginning,” Usher added. “He was the driving force of deception and evil and all of the things that turned A-Train away from who he thought he'd be into what he had become. And the fact that he was able to face off with that before seeing his end was just the greatest, most poetic ending that I think that character possibly could have had.”Antony Starr as Homelander on the season five premiere of "The Boys."Jasper Savage/Prime VideoStarr teased that A-Train’s death will exacerbate Homelander’s unraveling psyche in the upcoming episodes.“When I read it, I was like, ‘No, Jessie!’ because I love the guy and I’m fond of him,” Starr said. “I love the character. I think his character is one of the most compelling in the show, the journey he's been on. That said, I'm glad it was me because of what it does for the story. It had to be someone who would matter, to really set the ball rolling for the rest of the season.”Forbes‘The Boys’ Season 5, Episode 2 Recap: Soldier Boy’s Return Complicates ThingsBy Olivia Singh“I think there’s a lot of factors in this downward spiral of Homelander, and one of them is A-Train, in a big way, because Homelander is so oblivious and so unable to look inside himself, he cannot understand why people keep betraying him and what it is that is making all of this happen to him, and why this is happening to him,” Kripke said in a separate interview. “He doesn’t realize that it's obviously all his fault.”Chace Crawford as The Deep, Antony Starr as Homelander and Nathan Mitchell as Black Noir on season five of "The Boys."Jasper Savage/Prime VideoIt’s a testament to the show’s fearlessness that The Boys is willing to kill off a major, beloved character, especially so early in the final season. Kripke said that A-Train’s death serves as a warning to audiences that the final episodes won’t hold back. “I was actually a little nervous about killing off A-Train in the first episode,” the Boys creator said. “We had broken out a story for him, and the original plan, I think, was about episode three or so. I give credit to the writers, they sort of challenged me on it and they said, 'You keep saying that nobody’s safe. We have to prove it. You have to prove that, as early as the first episode, you’re not afraid to drop a main character because then everyone is at risk for the rest of the season.' And they were totally right.”Forbes‘The Boys’ Cast Teases ‘A Big MacGuffin’ And ‘Closure’ For Fans In The Final SeasonBy Olivia SinghThe Boys season five, episode one is streaming on Prime Video.
